pure-announcement.rationale: A sourced analysis answering whether site owners should adopt llms.txt, not any kind of launch or funding notice.

duplicate.rationale: None of the supplied nearest concepts covers llms.txt; the corpus's only llms.txt text is a rubric exemplar under .kb/exemplars, not a concept note a reader could have learned this from.

unfalsifiable.rationale: Every load-bearing claim links a primary source — Google's two AI-search docs, OpenAI's crawler documentation, and named on-record statements from the Search team.

durability.rationale: Its subject matches the rubric's own weak-durability anchor: an unadopted proposal whose evidence base (doc dates, on-record quotes, disputed crawler logs) will shift within months even if the no-provider-commitment conclusion holds.

actionability.rationale: It gives a site owner a direct decision rule — skip it for Google visibility, treat it as a cheap noindexed experiment for agent traffic, measure citations instead — grounded in the cited record.

atomicity.rationale: One question, one verdict: llms.txt is not an AI-search ranking lever; its real use is as an agent-facing documentation index.
